label: Input is one of d/i/r/f/a/0/s/l/x/m/c after k/n/u/q/v/2/e/p tokens appeared earlier
explanation: Mostly driven by the current input token: it fires on a set of about 11 tokens, d strongest (39% of d steps, 24% of mass), then i, r, f, a, 0, s, l, x, m, c. These tokens account for about 96% of activation mass. Whether it fires depends on which tokens came earlier: it is much more likely when tokens from a second set (k, n, u, q, v, 2, e, p) have already appeared, e.g. d right after k or u (the top examples are d/r/f/i following sequences of k, u, n, e, v). It fires in both the original and copy phases (roughly half the mass each), with a bump at the first copy step (recall_idx 1, right after <DEL>), and almost never at the delimiter step itself. Requiring at least 2 earlier context tokens raises mass recall to about 0.79, but precision stays near 0.25: many trigger tokens with that context still stay silent, so the exact history dependence is not captured. Magnitude is largest for d. Does not fire on <DEL> or (much) on k/n/u/e-type tokens themselves.
